transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I drive a cab, and even when I know for a fact I did my safety check on the car, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something. 

I keep thinking that because I missed something, somebody could get hurt, or my boss will say I lied about doing the inspection. I just can't make the thought shut up. It's constantly in my head while I'm driving, or even when I'm just at home trying to study. It's getting really hard to deal with.

When these thoughts occur, do you feel an urge to perform any specific actions or mental routines, like checking the car multiple times or repeating certain phrases in your head, to try and get rid of the worry?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I can even take a ride, I end up going around the car checking the tires, the lights, the doors... the meter and all my paperwork. And I just do it over and over. 

Sometimes I even take pictures of everything on my phone just to be sure. If something doesn't feel right while I'm doing it, I have to restart the whole check from the beginning. It's really frustrating because I'll be doing it even when passengers are literally standing there waiting for me, and I'm already late. I just have to do it anyway.
